items.title: ratatui::Scrollbar migration
items.problem: tui/render/scrollbar.rs hand-rolls a vertical scrollbar widget (render_scrollbar_gutter_visible, thumb_range_visible) when ratatui 0.30 ships a built-in ratatui::widgets::Scrollbar + ScrollbarState. The renderer (chrome.rs::render_scrollbars) is the only consumer. Migrating is mostly a renderer rewrite; keep SCROLLBAR_GUTTER, scrollbar_rect, thumb_range_visible (math used for track-click), track_click_to_scroll (mouse hit-test), and measure_paragraph_height (M167 detail scrollbar — unrelated to widget identity).
items.done_when: render_scrollbars constructs ratatui::widgets::Scrollbar + ScrollbarState per ScrollbarHitArea and renders via the framework; the home-rolled render_scrollbar_gutter_visible helper is gone from scrollbar.rs; tests + clippy + fmt all green.

Update tui/render/chrome.rs::render_scrollbars to construct the framework widget + ScrollbarState per ScrollbarHitArea.
Adapt tui_scrollbar.rs tests to drive the framework widget via a test helper (draw_scrollbar_for_test).
Drop the home-rolled scrollbar buffer writer; keep the math helpers (SCROLLBAR_GUTTER, scrollbar_rect, thumb_range_visible, track_click_to_scroll) and M167's measure_paragraph_height for callers.

items.title: Settings: flat list with section tags + help box
items.problem: The current Settings modal has a two-level outer/inner focus (Sections → Fields) and a separate field-edit popup. The outer modal already lives in the lane pane (M168) but the navigation model is still modal-flavoured. The Inbox model — flat list with kind prefix and one action per item — is a cleaner shape: drop the Sections-level focus, lay every key out flat with [section] on the left, surface per-key prose in a 3-row help box at the top, and use a single focus state (SelectedIdx) over the flat list. Enter opens the value-edit popup, Esc closes, ArrowUp/Down navigate.
items.done_when: render_settings_overlay paints a flat list of every key with [section] on the left, a 3-row help box at the top showing prose for the cursor row, and a single SelectedIdx focus. No Sections/Fields focus toggle. Enter opens the existing field-edit popup, Esc closes, ArrowUp/Down navigate. SETTINGS_SECTIONS still groups the data so the flat list keeps section tags in order; the help table is hard-coded in a new settings/help.rs.

items.title: Settings: group rows by section
items.problem: The current Settings flat list prints every row with [section] ui.key = value. For long sections (keybinds.* has 25 keys) the [keybinds] prefix repeats 25 times and the list is hard to scan. The Overview lane groups by 'kind' with a header per group; the Settings pane should match. Group the flat list by section in the renderer (one section header row before each section's keys, like the Inbox shape), and re-anchor the cursor navigation so 'Up' from the first key of a section doesn't try to move into the section header row.
items.done_when: render_settings_overlay groups keys by section: section header rows interleaved with key rows, the [section] inline prefix removed (section only appears as a header once per group), and the cursor navigation skips the section header rows automatically. The flat-list data shape (SETTINGS_KEYS) is unchanged — the grouping is render-only.
items.verification: cargo nextest run -p raul --no-fail-fast (the existing 480 tests stay green; new m168_settings_grouped tests for the section-header shape pass). cargo clippy -p raul --tests --no-deps -- -D warnings. cargo fmt --all -- --check. mp validate.
steps: In render_settings_overlay (crates/raul/src/tui/render/overlays.rs), build the flat-list items as a sequence of (row_kind, payload) entries where row_kind ∈ {Section, Key} instead of one List<ListItem> per key. Section rows render `--- section ---` (the user's `--- ui ---` shape) as styled non-interactive headers; Key rows render the same `[section] key = value` content as today (or drop the [section] prefix now that the section header carries it).

Convert the cursor navigation: when the cursor rests on a Key row, Up/Down skip Section rows automatically (they pass through to the next Key row). PageUp/PageDown operate on the Key subsequence, not the full interleaved list.
Update the smooth-scroll offset to count only Key rows (not Section rows) when computing the visible window, so the cursor never lands on a section header.

Add `crates/raul/tests/m168_settings_grouped.rs` with: a rendering test for the `--- section ---` header shape; a navigation test confirming Up/Down skip section headers; a no-row-padding test confirming the visible window counts only Key rows. Update `m168_settings.rs::flat_list_renders_all_keys_with_section_tag` (the [section] prefix per row may disappear or stay — either is fine; pick whatever reads cleanest).

items.title: Settings mode hotkeys: Esc closes, Tab→Overview, h ignored
items.problem: Three UX papercuts when the Settings modal is open: (1) When the field-edit popup is up, Esc closes the popup but leaves the modal up; another Esc closes the modal — confusing two-step. (2) When the user is in the Settings modal, the Tab key gets routed through PushInputChar ('\t') as a literal tab character into the buffer, instead of jumping lanes. (3) The 'h' key still triggers hide_done (ToggleHideDone) even while the Settings modal is open, leaving the user's list pane state confused. All three should be hijacked while the Settings modal is up.
items.done_when: modes::settings::handle_key intercepts three global hotkeys BEFORE the field/buffer dispatch: Esc closes the modal (when not editing the buffer, single-press; when editing the buffer, single-press first closes the edit popup and the same key event sequence is recognized, the modal is closed by a repeated Esc; see below). Tab maps to JumpLane(0) (Overview). 'h' (the hide_done binding) is a no-op while Settings is open. The field-edit buffer continues to receive Esc / Tab / h as input characters when the edit popup is up (input mode takes precedence over the global hijack, so editing a value still works).
items.verification: cargo nextest run -p raul --no-fail-fast (the existing 484 tests stay green; new m168_settings_hotkeys tests pass). cargo clippy -p raul --tests --no-deps -- -D warnings. cargo fmt --all -- --check. mp validate.
steps: In `modes::settings::handle_key`, intercept three global hotkeys BEFORE the field-edit dispatch: Esc always closes the modal (single press, even from the edit popup — pop the popup if up, then drop the modal). Tab maps to JumpLane(0) (Overview) regardless of the current lane. 'h' (the default keybinds.hide_done binding) becomes a no-op while Settings is open.

Keep the input-char handling intact: while the edit popup is up, all printable characters still route to `state.edit.buffer` (the existing PushInputChar path). The hotkey hijack is only for Esc / Tab / h, which the field-edit handler also dispatches via PushInputChar ('\t' for Tab, '\x1b' for Esc) — make sure the hijack runs BEFORE that so Esc/Tab don't enter the buffer.

Add `crates/raul/tests/m168_settings_hotkeys.rs` with: a test that Esc with edit-popup up closes both (popup + modal); a test that Tab with edit-popup up jumps to Overview (state.active_lane == Overview); a test that 'h' inside the modal is a no-op (state.hide_done unchanged); a regression test that printable characters still enter the buffer.
Update `tui_settings.rs::navigate_sections_and_fields` to test the new Tab-jumps-to-Overview behavior (the test currently uses Down/Up, swap one assertion to Tab).
items.evidence: cargo nextest run -p raul --no-fail-fast: 490/490 passed (added 6 new hotkey tests in m168_settings_hotkeys). cargo clippy -p raul --tests --no-deps -- -D warnings: clean. cargo fmt --all -- --check: clean. mp validate: clean. modes::settings::handle_key now intercepts Esc / Tab / h BEFORE the field-edit dispatch: Esc always closes the modal in a single press (regardless of edit popup state); Tab/Shift+Tab map to JumpLane(0) (Overview) via the literal KeyCode::Tab / KeyCode::BackTab match; 'h' (the default keybinds.hide_done binding) is a no-op while Settings is open. All printable characters still route to the input buffer. The _state reference is captured once via 'let Mode::Settings(_state) = &app.active_mode' to avoid mut-borrow churn across the early-return branches.

items.title: mp autopilot: codify the four-tier git commit strategy
items.problem: Per mp-herdr-log.txt's "OPEN DECISION: git commit strategy" — ad-hoc per-cycle/commit patterns across M200/M201/M202 produced (a)  metadata drift when findings are grouped into one commit, and (b) evidence-overwrite by completion-summary commits (recurring across M200 F-12, M201 F-05, M202 F-13). The four-tier commit policy proposed in the log: (1) per-step implementation commits; (2) per-finding fix commits (NEVER grouped, so  is unambiguous); (3) lifecycle-evidence meta-commits (no code changes); (4) per-AC evidence restoration via  (NEVER overwriting via generic summary commits). Each test-fixture commit must match the pattern: type=messages describe (1)+(2) as the only commits that touch code or evidence fields.
items.done_when: A docs/mp/commit-strategy.md note codifies the four tiers; a regression test in crates/mp/tests/ validates that no commit in the test fixture combines an evidence-field write with a code change; the lint rule enforces the policy at commit time (or via CI).
items.verification: manual: reviewed on completion; the regression test fails if a fixture commit combines code changes with acceptance_criteria[].evidence writes; cargo nextest run -p mp --test commit_strategy_policy --no-fail-fast; cargo clippy -p mp --tests --no-deps -- -D warnings; cargo fmt --all -- --check.

items.title: mp: per-milestone folder migration (spec.json + findings.json + lifecycle.json + reviews.json + runner_notes.json + dependencies.json)
items.problem: Per mp-herdr-log.txt's "OPEN DECISION: milestone document structure" — today's milestone state is fragmented across master-plan/milestones/<id>-*.json + master-plan/reviews.json + master-plan/activity.json + master-plan/backlog.json + master-plan/decisions.json. The log's recommendation: per-milestone folder at master-plan/milestones/<id>/ containing spec.json (moved from the current single file), findings.json (extracted from reviews.json), lifecycle.json (extracted from activity.json filtered by subject), runner_notes.json (already supported after M207 AC-04), dependencies.json (the planned / from the spec), reviews.json (per-cycle summaries). One folder = one milestone; everything discoverable from a single grep; per-milestone git diffs become natural. Migration must keep existing milestones discoverable (back-compat reads). Phase 1 adds folder support alongside current files. Phase 2 migrates findings + lifecycle to per-milestone files. Phase 3 deprecates the global indexes' per-milestone content.

items.title: mp autopilot: codify the four-tier git commit strategy
items.problem: Per mp-herdr-log.txt's 'OPEN DECISION: git commit strategy' — ad-hoc per-cycle/commit patterns across M200/M201/M202 produced (a) `fixed_in` metadata drift when findings are grouped into one commit, and (b) evidence-overwrite by completion-summary commits (recurring across M200 F-12, M201 F-05, M202 F-13). The four-tier commit policy proposed in the log: (1) per-step implementation commits; (2) per-finding fix commits (NEVER grouped, so `fixed_in` is unambiguous); (3) lifecycle-evidence meta-commits (no code changes); (4) per-AC evidence restoration via `mp milestone criterion pass <AC> --evidence` (NEVER overwriting via generic summary commits). Each test-fixture commit must match the pattern: type=messages describe (1)+(2) as the only commits that touch code or evidence fields.
items.done_when: A `docs/mp/commit-strategy.md` note codifies the four tiers; a regression test in `crates/mp/tests/` validates that no commit in the test fixture combines an evidence-field write with a code change; the lint rule enforces the policy at commit time (or via CI).
items.verification: manual: reviewed on completion; the regression test fails if a fixture commit combines code changes with `acceptance_criteria[].evidence` writes; `cargo nextest run -p mp --test commit_strategy_policy --no-fail-fast`; `cargo clippy -p mp --tests --no-deps -- -D warnings`; `cargo fmt --all -- --check`.
